- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.4) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and price is trending upward, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; apply +0.5–1.0% bias to early horizon.
- When sentiment is high and price is near recent high, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid premature mean reversion.
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 0.0–0.2) and price is rising, model underestimates; apply +1–2% bias to forecast to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
